newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges outside countries not to fight in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges outside countries not to fight in Zaire.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday urged all outside countries and "mercenary groups" not to take part into the fighting in Eastern Zaire, saying that would further escalate the fighting and cause more civilian deaths.

"The United States has consistently urged other nations not to become involved in the fighting in Eastern Zaire. We will continue to discourage actively any outside country, any outside group of foreigners or mercenary groups (from involvement)," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told a regular department briefing.
"We would discourage them from...entering into the conflagration in eastern Zaire because that would escalate the fighting and contribute to further civilian deaths."
Zaire accuses Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi of fighting alongside ethnic Tutsi rebels who have captured strategic towns in Eastern Zaire and who say their goal is to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.

A senior Zaire Defence Ministry official told Reuters on Monday that Togo, Chad and Morocco had accepted a request by Mobutu for troops to support him, while Egypt agreed to send war materials. Togo, however, denied planning to send troops and Egypt said it had no defence ties with Zaire.
Burns said the United States had "ample evidence" of the participation of foreign forces in the fighting, but he declined to name the countries involved.
"We have reminded the governments that border Zaire that we do not support this in any way," he said, stressing that Washington "supports the territorial integrity of Zaire."
